title: Nosebleeds
intro: Nosebleeds are common and usually harmless, caused by small blood vessels near the front of the nose breaking. They look alarming but can almost always be stopped at home within minutes. Knowing the right technique and when to seek help makes them much less frightening.

sections.heading: Causes
paragraphs: Common causes include dry air, nose picking, colds and allergies that irritate the lining, minor injury, forceful nose blowing and some nasal sprays. Blood thinners, high blood pressure, clotting disorders and alcohol can contribute or make bleeding harder to stop.

sections.heading: How to stop a nosebleed
paragraphs: Sit upright and lean slightly forward so that blood does not run down the throat. Pinch the soft part of the nose, just below the bony bridge, firmly and breathe through your mouth. Keep pinching continuously for ten to fifteen minutes without checking. Spit out any blood in the mouth. Do not tilt the head back or lie down.

sections.heading: After the bleeding stops
paragraphs: Avoid blowing your nose, picking, heavy lifting, hot drinks and strenuous activity for about a day to allow the clot to settle. Apply petroleum jelly or saline gel inside the nostril to keep it moist, and use a humidifier in dry rooms.

sections.heading: When to seek help
paragraphs: Get medical help if bleeding lasts more than twenty minutes, is heavy, follows a head injury, occurs with dizziness or fainting, or happens repeatedly. Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners. Doctors may seal the vessel or pack the nose. Frequent nosebleeds in children are usually harmless but can be assessed.

sections.heading: Prevention
paragraphs: Keep the nose moist, trim children's nails, avoid picking, treat allergies and manage blood pressure. Aim nasal sprays away from the middle wall of the nose.

examples.title: Helping a child
examples.text: Imagine your child has a nosebleed at school. You could calmly have them sit leaning forward, pinch their nose for ten minutes and avoid lying down or tilting back.

examples.title: Preventing recurrence
examples.text: Suppose you get nosebleeds every winter. You might use saline gel nightly, run a humidifier and ask your doctor to check your nose if bleeding continues.
